C0.quote: an early criticism of Plurality rule and, in search of a better method
C0.note: Historical paper, but its object is the plurality voting procedure and early pairwise-comparison ideas. Coded ELIG because the object is a voting procedure.

C1.quote: we present two texts that add two more early appearances
C1.note: History-of-ideas study of two Roman texts; no formal results.

C2.1.quote: Plurality rule by categoric vote does not allow to change the parts

C2.2.quote: each voter votes for one candidate and the candidate with the highest number
C2.2.note: Single-choice plurality vote (one alternative per judge); fits none of the listed formats.

C2.3.quote: the pulse of the actual preferences of the voters

C2.4.quote: the real will (or preference) of the judges has not been properly reflected
C2.4.note: Votes (the 'parts') are contrasted with the voters' actual preferences.

C3.1.quote: supporters of "death" strategically voted in favor of the "exile" alternative
C3.1.note: Strategic voting appears only in the historical narrative of Pliny's episode, not as an analysis the paper carries out.

C3.2.note: The paper never says that judges submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH and the paper uses no voter utility notion.

C5.1.quote: it fails to correctly represent the will of the judges
C5.1.note: Normative evaluation of plurality by representation of the judges' will, in the body of the paper.

C5.2.quote: the actual preferences of the voters, rather than the parts formed
C5.2.note: Evaluated against the judges' will or preferences, which are distinct from the votes.

VOT.quote_behav: supporters of "death" strategically voted in favor of the "exile" alternative
VOT.note: Senators in Pliny's episode vote strategically. The judges in the Declamation and Gellius cases are given fixed votes. There is no formal model.

ORG.quote_behav: Pliny, who advocated for acquittal and was aware of the strength
ORG.quote_info: was aware of the strength of each group
ORG.note: Pliny, chairing the Senate, changes the voting procedure. Present only in the historical episode, not in a formal model.

C7.1.quote: supporters of "death" strategically voted in favor of the "exile" alternative
C7.1.note: In Pliny's episode both the chair (ORG) and the voters are strategic. The non-strategic judges appear only in the separate Declamation and Gellius cases.

C8.1.quote: supporters of "death" strategically voted in favor of the "exile" alternative
C8.1.note: No solution concept is used. Strategic behaviour is only narrated historically.

claims.quote: has evident failures that have triggered theoretical reflection from remote times
find more robust and fair alternatives
this intuition conceals the numerous flaws inherent in Plurality

C9.1.note: Claims about the flaws of plurality and the search for fairer methods.

C9.2.note: The claim that plurality is flawed or unfair needs a statement of how submitted votes relate to the judges' preferences and what the judges know, and the paper gives none. It treats the judges' preferences as unobserved and the votes as 'parts'.

C10.1.note: The paper does not state a procedural-only reading.
